n1.summary: Runs the orders and profile queries at the same time, then summarizes; results are cached for 30 s per user.

n2.summary: New GET /dashboard/{user_id} route; delegates everything to load_dashboard.

n3.summary: Builds a decorator that keeps each result in a dict for `ttl` seconds, keyed by the call arguments.

n4.summary: Opens a session, fetches the user's orders, closes the session.

n5.summary: Opens its own session and fetches the profile, in parallel with fetch_orders.

n6.summary: Counts orders and collects the ids of those over 100.

py.mutableDefault.here: highlights=[] is created once: every dashboard call appends to the same list, so ids from other users leak in.

py.asyncAwait.here: Each await hands control back to the loop while the database answers.

py.decorator.here: @cached(ttl=30) replaces load_dashboard with the wrapper built in cache.py.

py.contextManager.here: get_session closes the session even if the query raises.

py.gather.here: Both queries run concurrently: total time is the slower one, not the sum. One failure cancels the result.

watch.text: highlights=[] is shared across calls: use None, create the list inside

fundamental.text: gather starts both queries, then the loop switches between them at each await. That is why the two sessions overlap in time.
